VALUATION_METHODS._AdditionalDescription: GENERAL MARKET & ECONOMIC CONDITION IN UTAH: As reported by the Utah State Governor's office and Utah Department of Workforce Services updated September 2022. Employment Change: Utah’s nonagricultural employment was the 20th most favorable in with an increase of 3.4% compared to the nationally, employment growth of 3.8%. Unemployment: Utah’s August 2022 unemployment rate is the 2rd lowest in the nation at 2.0% and better than the national unemployment rate of 3.7%. Workforce: Utah has the 6th highest labor force participation rate in the US. Household Income: Utah’s household income is 5th highest in the nation at $83,670 compared to the US $67,521. Poverty Rate: poverty level is the 2nd lowest in the nation at 7.1%. Demographic: Utah has the youngest median age at 31.3 years old compared to the national median age of 38.2 years old. Utah also has the largest household size at 3.08 compared to the national household size of 2.61. Home Prices: According to the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) House Price Appreciation Ranking, Utah’s house prices were up 26.5% in the Third quarter of 2022 from the Third quarter of 2020. Median home sale price in Utah is $497,100 and the Ogden-Clearfield MSA has a median home sale price of $434,400 (+24%). Logan, MSA has a median home sale price of 417,9000 (+30.6%) Building Permits: The top five counties building permit in 2021 were Salt Lake (8,862), Utah (10,894), Washington (3,297, Davis (3,367) and Weber (1,658). Interest Rates: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.75% for the week ending Oct 7, 2022, Foreclosure Rates: As reported by RealtyTrac Utah has an average foreclosure rate of 0.008%, The Utah foreclosure rate is higher than the national average of 0.0149%. Coincident Index: Utah’s July 2022 Coincident index was 165.8 which is the largest (best) in the nation. The national coincident index for Aug 2022 was 135.16. The coincident indexes combine four state-level indicators to summarize current economic conditions in a single statistic. The four state-level variables in each coincident index are nonfarm payroll employment, average hours worked in manufacturing by production workers, the unemployment rate, and wage and salary disbursements plus proprietors' income deflated by the consumer price index (U.S. city average). The trend for each state’s index is set to the trend of its gross domestic product (GDP), so long-term growth in the state’s index matches long-term growth in its GDP.

SALES_COMPARISON._Comment: The comparable sales selected are the most similar disclosed sales. Adjustments reflect the different features as valued by the market and not the cost of the amenity. Typically these differences included: size, parking, baths, fireplaces, jetted tubs, out buildings, etc. Differences in GLA were adjusted $80p/sf, which was derived as follows: Replacement cost new (Marshal&Swift/Local builder) less physical depreciation (ref to cost apprch) less market difference of 60% ($204.63-%=$204.63-60%=$81.85 ($80r) basement shell at $45p/sf and finish by room count for utility rather than percent of finish. The number of rooms contribute more to value than does the percentage of finish and real estate agents tend to more accurately report the number of finished rooms than correctly estimating the percent of finish. Adjusted value range from sales comparison approach is $660,000 to $702,000(r) See additional comps and comments on next page. See comments on page 3. An attempt was made to bracket all areas of value as the market determines, i.e garage, fireplace, cooling, age, lot size & utility etc. Comparable provided as a bracketing comparable. Comps #5 & #6 are current active listings provided as part of clients scope of work. No consideration was given these listings as they are not closed sales. In the opinion of this appraiser the comparable sales presented best represent the subjects value.
